title: Stoma site marking before resection with possible stoma
logic: If a colorectal resection is booked where a stoma is planned or reasonably possible (Hartmann's, low anterior resection, emergency colectomy), and no preoperative stoma site marking is documented, the booking is incomplete.
action: Flag the theatre booking; prompt stoma-site marking and counselling by the most stoma-experienced available clinician; allow documented override only for immediate life-threat emergencies.

title: Histology and staging before elective cancer resection
logic: If an elective colorectal cancer resection is booked without recorded tissue diagnosis and staging imaging (CT chest-abdomen-pelvis or best available equivalent), the case does not meet MDT-readiness criteria.
action: Block elective listing until histology and staging records are attached, or a senior surgeon documents why the case must proceed without them (e.g. obstructing tumour treated as urgent).

title: Rectal cancer mandates MDT before resection
logic: If a confirmed or suspected rectal adenocarcinoma is on a surgical pathway and no multidisciplinary team decision is recorded, the case is classified as MDT-pending and must not proceed to resection, because neoadjuvant therapy may change the operation or avoid it.
action: Route the case to the central hospital colorectal MDT worklist; hold elective resection booking until an MDT outcome is recorded; emergency obstruction may be defunctioned with a stoma without waiting for MDT.

title: Anastomotic leak pattern after colorectal anastomosis
logic: If a patient between postoperative day 2 and day 7 of a colorectal anastomosis develops sustained tachycardia above 100, new atrial fibrillation, fever, rising inflammatory markers, increasing abdominal pain, or faeculent/purulent drain output, anastomotic leak is the presumed diagnosis until excluded.
action: Raise a danger-sign alert; senior surgical review within 1 hour; recommend contrast CT where available or return to theatre on clinical grounds where imaging is not accessible; do not start anticoagulation for new atrial fibrillation without considering leak as the driver.

title: Failed or bloody volvulus decompression is gangrene until proven otherwise
logic: If endoscopic detorsion of sigmoid volvulus fails, returns blood or dark mucosa, or the patient has peritonism or systemic toxicity, gangrenous bowel is presumed.
action: Escalate to EMERGENCY laparotomy pathway immediately; do not repeat decompression attempts or observe overnight.

title: Colorectal antibiotic prophylaxis covers anaerobes
logic: If any colorectal procedure opening or resecting large bowel is booked, prophylaxis must cover both aerobic gram-negative organisms and anaerobes: intravenous cefazolin (or ceftriaxone per local policy) plus metronidazole within 60 minutes before incision, with intra-operative redosing for prolonged cases per agent half-life.
action: Prompt combination prophylaxis at induction with timing capture; alert if metronidazole is missing from a colorectal booking's prophylaxis plan; convert to treatment course when established peritonitis is coded.

title: New stoma viability and output surveillance
logic: If a new stoma is formed, stoma colour, spout, and output must be recorded at least once per nursing shift for the first 48 hours; a dusky or black stoma, no output beyond 24–48 hours with distension, or high output above 1500 ml/day each require escalation.
action: Generate per-shift stoma observation tasks for 48 hours then daily; alert the surgical team on dusky/black colour (possible ischaemia), absent output with distension (possible obstruction), or sustained high output (fluid and electrolyte replacement plan needed).

title: Post-resection colorectal cancer surveillance
logic: If a patient has completed curative colorectal cancer resection, surveillance follows: clinical review with CEA where available every 6 months for 3 years then annually to 5 years; colonoscopy at 1 year post-resection (or completion colonoscopy within 6 months if the colon was obstructed and not fully evaluated preoperatively), then per findings; imaging per MDT plan.
action: Auto-generate the surveillance schedule at histology sign-off; book the 1-year (or 6-month completion) colonoscopy; flag missed surveillance events to the responsible clinic.

title: Perianal abscess needs a fistula check
logic: If a perianal abscess was drained, a dedicated review at about 6 weeks is required to detect fistula-in-ano, which develops in a large minority; persistent discharge at review indicates a track.
action: Auto-book the 6-week review at drainage; if discharge or recurrent sepsis is recorded, route to EUA listing; prompt diabetes screening and HIV test offer at the same review if not already recorded.
